script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The text places the door work in Hezekiah's first month, but does not say it was the first thing on his list or that he did it before anything else.
Repairing the doors does not establish that they stayed exactly where they were or rule out their being taken down during the work.
The explanation puts removal of impurity after consecration of the house. The passage describes cleansing the house as part of its consecration, not as a separate step afterward.
The text says the fathers did not present burnt offerings in the Holy Place. It does not say offerings were physically missing from it.
The text does not establish whether Hezekiah is telling the Levites news.
Saying Hezekiah is not turning toward a plan of his own adds a contrast the text does not make. He says making a covenant is in his heart.
The geographical description of Assyria is information from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not establish that Hezekiah never made this battle plan. It also says more than that his entire speech concerns the house and the covenant.
The identification of Edom as a neighboring nation is information from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the answer and verse, without a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
1 Samuel 17:2 places the Israelites in the Valley of Elah, but does not itself describe David meeting Goliath. The reference needs to include the later verses that do.
The explanation is generic, and its closing comparison merely repeats that sixteen is less than twenty.
The text says the articles are in front of the altar, but does not say that was their former place.
The statement that oil appears elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference or should be removed.
The passage does not place the Levites on one side and the priests on the other.
The passage does not say the noise stops or describe this as a quiet moment after a loud one.
The passage says the king and those present bow and worship; it does not say nobody heads home or that everyone stays in the same place.
The text says those whose hearts were willing brought burnt offerings. It does not say nobody was dragged to the altar.
The identification of Benjamites with the tribe of Benjamin is information from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The identification of Ephraimites with the tribe of Ephraim is information from outside the passage and needs a reference.
